title: Security incident management and cyber resilience
summary: Coordinate a fact-based response that protects people, preserves evidence and restores trustworthy service.
outcomes: Triage and escalate a suspected incident.
Coordinate technical, business, privacy and communications decisions.
Validate recovery and convert lessons into owned improvements.

realExample.title: Transnet restores the NAVIS N4 terminal system
realExample.documentedOutcome: The 29 July 2021 government statement reported restoration of the NAVIS N4 terminal operating system following the 22 July cyber incident.
realExample.discussion: Examine the decisions needed between detecting disruption and declaring a public-facing service recovered: containment, coordination, trusted systems, transaction reconciliation and communication.
realExample.scope: A documented restoration outcome. Preliminary statements about data impact should not be treated as a final forensic finding.

units.title: Triage, contain and coordinate
objectives: Distinguish an alert from a confirmed incident.
Make timely containment decisions with service owners.
Maintain a usable incident chronology and notification route.

chapters.title: Start with what is known
chapters.bodyHtml:
An alert is a signal requiring assessment. An incident is an event or condition that breaches or threatens the relevant security and service requirements. The initial record should say what was observed, when, by whom, which service may be affected and what remains unknown.

Use a triage method based on consequence and urgency. A suspicious login to a test account and evidence of payment-file alteration require different responses. Consider affected people, privilege, spread, critical service deadlines and the ability to contain harm.

Assign an incident lead and contact route. Preserve the original report and important times, including time zones. Avoid replacing earlier observations with a later narrative; a chronology should show how understanding changed and which decisions were made on each basis.

chapters.title: Contain harm while protecting the service
chapters.bodyHtml:
Containment can include restricting a compromised account, isolating affected components or suspending a risky interface through authorised technical action. The choice should consider continuing harm, service consequences and evidence preservation.

The DISO coordinates the security view but should not improvise destructive technical steps outside the response team's authority. Unplanned wiping or rebuilding can destroy evidence and leave the underlying compromise unresolved. Bring in the responsible technical and investigative roles.

Where essential service must continue, agree a controlled alternative. Record who authorises it, what information it uses, how transactions are tracked and how they will later be reconciled. A manual workaround can preserve service while creating new integrity or privacy risks that need control.

chapters.title: Run parallel decision streams
chapters.bodyHtml:
Technical containment, business continuity, legal/privacy assessment and public communication need coordination, but one stream should not unnecessarily wait for every other stream to finish. The incident lead should keep owners aligned around a shared factual record.

Assess notification through the responsible roles using the applicable legal trigger and current receiving route. A supplier's internal report is not automatically the department's completed notification. Record decisions, submissions, affected-person communication and later updates.

Use clear internal updates: confirmed facts, working hypotheses, service impact, actions, decisions needed and next update time. Restrict sensitive details to the people who need them. Consistent communication supports action without pretending that uncertainty has disappeared.

application.title: Run the first hour of a fictional incident
application.instructionsHtml:
At 09:00 a clerk reports that the payment system shows unfamiliar bank changes. At 09:10 ICT finds suspicious use of a supplier administrator account. At 09:20 the supplier asks for unrestricted access to investigate. A relief-payment batch is due at 10:00.

Spend about 60 minutes producing a first-hour incident log, containment decision, service alternative and legal/privacy notification work allocation.
application.deliverable: An incident chronology and four coordinated decision records.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Record facts and unknowns separately. Preserve the suspicious changes and access evidence; confirm the state of the payment batch before release or retry.

Route restricted investigative access through the incident authority. Consider pausing affected payments with a controlled urgent-service alternative rather than giving unrestricted access by default.

Assign privacy/legal assessment promptly, prepare factual notifications where required and state the next update time. Do not wait for a final forensic report to begin the relevant decision process.

reflection.prompt: Who would coordinate a supplier, service owner and privacy officer at 09:00 on a public holiday?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Describe the actual role/deputy arrangement your department should maintain.

quiz.title: Triage, contain and coordinate — knowledge check

questions.name: M09-U01-Q01
questions.promptHtml: A suspicious login alert has not yet been investigated. How should it be described?

answers.textHtml: An observed alert with its known facts and unresolved significance
answers.feedbackHtml: Triage starts with an accurate description.

answers.textHtml: A confirmed data theft in every system
answers.feedbackHtml: That exceeds the evidence.

answers.textHtml: Proof of harmless activity because no complaint exists
answers.feedbackHtml: Absence of a complaint does not resolve it.

answers.textHtml: A reason to discard the log
answers.feedbackHtml: The log may be important.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Triage starts with an accurate description.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q02
questions.promptHtml: Which factor most increases urgency in the payment scenario?

answers.textHtml: Possible unauthorised changes before an imminent batch release
answers.feedbackHtml: Prioritise consequence, exposure and time.

answers.textHtml: That an incident ticket was filed using last year's template
answers.feedbackHtml: Template age does not establish immediate payment exposure.

answers.textHtml: That the supplier prefers a meeting after the batch deadline
answers.feedbackHtml: Supplier convenience does not determine the urgency of the service risk.

answers.textHtml: That the warning was copied to many senior recipients
answers.feedbackHtml: Distribution size is not the relevant exposure or time constraint.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Prioritise consequence, exposure and time.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q03
questions.promptHtml: What is a risk of an unplanned immediate rebuild?

answers.textHtml: It may destroy evidence and leave the cause unresolved
answers.feedbackHtml: Use authorised response and preservation procedures.

answers.textHtml: That rebuilding automatically establishes a trustworthy recovery point
answers.feedbackHtml: A rebuild still needs validation of the data and recovery basis.

answers.textHtml: That a restored host automatically resolves the cause of compromise
answers.feedbackHtml: The underlying cause can remain unless investigated and corrected.

answers.textHtml: That restarting the service settles all external transaction states
answers.feedbackHtml: Business effects still require reconciliation.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Use authorised response and preservation procedures.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q04
questions.promptHtml: A supplier asks for unrestricted investigative access. What should govern the decision?

answers.textHtml: The incident need, authorised scope and controlled access method
answers.feedbackHtml: Support investigation through controlled authority.

answers.textHtml: The supplier's request alone
answers.feedbackHtml: The department must assess scope.

answers.textHtml: A permanent waiver of access control
answers.feedbackHtml: Investigation does not require unlimited continuing privilege.

answers.textHtml: A rule that no supplier can ever assist
answers.feedbackHtml: Appropriate authorised assistance may be necessary.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Support investigation through controlled authority.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q05
questions.promptHtml: What should a manual emergency payment process include?

answers.textHtml: Authorised transactions and a later reconciliation route
answers.feedbackHtml: Continuity measures need trustworthy records.

answers.textHtml: No records to save time
answers.feedbackHtml: That creates integrity and accountability risks.

answers.textHtml: A separate permanent process with no owner
answers.feedbackHtml: The workaround needs governance.

answers.textHtml: An assumption that every later retry is safe
answers.feedbackHtml: Effects must be reconciled.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Continuity measures need trustworthy records.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q06
questions.promptHtml: What should an incident update distinguish?

answers.textHtml: Confirmed facts, hypotheses, actions and decisions needed
answers.feedbackHtml: A shared factual picture supports coordination.

answers.textHtml: Only the most reassuring interpretation
answers.feedbackHtml: That can hide uncertainty.

answers.textHtml: Every rumour as a confirmed fact
answers.feedbackHtml: That misleads decisions.

answers.textHtml: Only technical details with no service impact
answers.feedbackHtml: Business owners need the consequence.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A shared factual picture supports coordination.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which records belong in the initial chronology? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Observation and discovery times
answers.feedbackHtml: They establish the sequence.

answers.textHtml: Service scope and what remains unknown
answers.feedbackHtml: They make the current assessment explicit.

answers.textHtml: A rewritten timeline that hides earlier uncertainty
answers.feedbackHtml: That removes useful history.

answers.textHtml: Unverified attribution stated as fact
answers.feedbackHtml: Attribution needs evidence.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Preserve how understanding develops.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which streams may need to proceed in parallel? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Technical containment and business continuity
answers.feedbackHtml: Both can be urgent.

answers.textHtml: Legal/privacy assessment and communications preparation
answers.feedbackHtml: They need current facts and owners.

answers.textHtml: Final forensic certainty before any decision
answers.feedbackHtml: Some decisions cannot wait for that.

answers.textHtml: Independent uncoordinated public statements from every team
answers.feedbackHtml: That fragments communication.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Parallel work should share one coherent factual record.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q09
questions.promptHtml: A supplier's notification to the department automatically proves the department notified the Regulator.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. These are distinct receiving events and responsibilities.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: These are distinct receiving events and responsibilities.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: These are distinct receiving events and responsibilities.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q10
questions.promptHtml: Containment choices can have service consequences that need an accountable decision.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Protecting against further harm and maintaining essential service must be considered together.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Protecting against further harm and maintaining essential service must be considered together.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Protecting against further harm and maintaining essential service must be considered together.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the response record to its purpose.

pairs.answer: Track observations and decisions over time

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The response needs linked but distinct records.

questions.name: M09-U01-Q12
questions.promptHtml: An incident update separates confirmed [[1]] from working [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: This keeps uncertainty visible without stopping action.

units.title: Recover with confidence and learn from the event
objectives: Coordinate accurate public and stakeholder messages.
Turn a review into delivered control improvements.

chapters.title: Recovery is more than a green screen
chapters.bodyHtml:
A system responding again is an important milestone, but the service owner needs to know whether its information and transactions are trustworthy. Check the recovery source, relevant access, configuration, interfaces and business records through the authorised recovery plan.

Reconcile work around the disruption: payments already sent, decisions entered manually, records changed during the incident and messages still queued. Avoid duplicating an action because its first response was lost. Retain the original identifiers and evidence where available.

The Transnet restoration report provides a real service-recovery outcome. In a classroom exercise, ask what conditions would support a department's own declaration of recovery. Do not infer a complete forensic conclusion from a public statement that reported a system restored.

chapters.title: Communicate what affected people can use
chapters.bodyHtml:
Public messages should identify the affected service, what people need to do, available alternatives and when another update will arrive. Use the authorised communications route and coordinate legal/privacy facts. Avoid revealing sensitive investigative details or giving reassurance beyond the evidence.

Correct information as understanding changes. Preserve the earlier message and issue a clear update rather than silently editing away a material error. A person deciding whether to submit a form or change a credential needs current, understandable instructions.

Communications also include staff, suppliers and partner agencies. They may need different operational detail but should receive compatible facts. Keep a named owner and an approved contact route for questions that cannot be answered immediately.

chapters.title: Review decisions and close the causes
chapters.bodyHtml:
The continuity Directive requires a post-implementation review after a disaster and an accountable return to normal operations. Review what happened, how decisions were made, what helped and which dependencies or controls failed.

Separate the immediate cause from contributing process conditions. A compromised credential may expose weaknesses in access scope, reset procedures, supplier governance and detection. Assign improvements that reach those causes, with owners and observable completion conditions.

Evaluate the response itself: contact accuracy, decision speed, public-service alternatives, evidence preservation and reconciliation. Retain successful practices too. A review that produces an unowned list does not improve resilience; completed changes and later exercises show whether the lessons became capability.

application.title: Decide whether the fictional relief service is recovered
application.instructionsHtml:
The portal is back online. ICT restored last night's database; Finance says one batch may have reached the bank; district staff recorded 120 urgent applications on paper; the incident's access path has been restricted but remains under investigation.

Spend about 60 minutes preparing recovery acceptance conditions, a public update and a five-action review plan.
application.deliverable: A recovery decision, short public message and owned improvement plan.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Confirm the bank batch before resend, reconcile paper applications and verify the restored data and permissions. State which services can resume and which need controlled handling.

Communicate available services and useful next steps without claiming the investigation is complete. Give an update time and contact route.

Assign improvements in supplier access, transaction recovery, alternative intake, contact arrangements and detection. Each needs an owner and evidence of a changed condition.

reflection.prompt: Which recovery declaration in your department would benefit from explicit business acceptance criteria?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Name the records and service outcomes that would need confirmation before normal operation resumes.

quiz.title: Recover with confidence and learn from the event — knowledge check

questions.name: M09-U02-Q01
questions.promptHtml: The portal is online after restore. What must still be established?

answers.textHtml: That required records, transactions and access are trustworthy
answers.feedbackHtml: Recovery includes business integrity and usable operation.

answers.textHtml: Only that the login endpoint responds successfully
answers.feedbackHtml: A responding page is a component observation, not complete service recovery.

answers.textHtml: Only that the restored server passes a basic health check
answers.feedbackHtml: Records, permissions and business transactions still need validation.

answers.textHtml: Only that the supplier has closed its infrastructure incident
answers.feedbackHtml: The department's service condition can extend beyond the supplier's component scope.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Recovery includes business integrity and usable operation.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q02
questions.promptHtml: A payment response was lost during the incident. What should precede resend?

answers.textHtml: Reconcile the original payment's actual state
answers.feedbackHtml: Use original identifiers and evidence to determine effects.

answers.textHtml: Assume the missing response means no payment occurred
answers.feedbackHtml: The action may have completed.

answers.textHtml: Create a new payment ID immediately
answers.feedbackHtml: That may produce duplication.

answers.textHtml: Ignore the beneficiary indefinitely
answers.feedbackHtml: The service still needs resolution.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Use original identifiers and evidence to determine effects.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q03
questions.promptHtml: What is the best public update while investigation continues?

answers.textHtml: State available services, known impact, useful actions and next update time
answers.feedbackHtml: Communicate useful facts within their known scope.

answers.textHtml: Claim no data was affected without evidence
answers.feedbackHtml: That exceeds known facts.

answers.textHtml: Publish sensitive investigative records
answers.feedbackHtml: That can cause further harm.

answers.textHtml: Provide no service information until every cause is known
answers.feedbackHtml: Affected people still need practical guidance.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Communicate useful facts within their known scope.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q04
questions.promptHtml: A material public statement was wrong. What should happen?

answers.textHtml: Issue a clear correction and preserve the message history
answers.feedbackHtml: Correct information transparently through the authorised route.

answers.textHtml: Replace the old message silently so readers cannot compare versions
answers.feedbackHtml: A clear correction lets affected people understand what changed.

answers.textHtml: Leave the statement unchanged until the entire investigation is final
answers.feedbackHtml: A material error can need correction before every cause is known.

answers.textHtml: Issue a different claim without identifying what was corrected
answers.feedbackHtml: This can leave recipients relying on the earlier wrong statement.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Correct information transparently through the authorised route.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q05
questions.promptHtml: What makes a post-incident action useful?

answers.textHtml: It changes a contributing condition and has an owner and completion evidence
answers.feedbackHtml: Lessons should become operating capability.

answers.textHtml: It repeats the incident title
answers.feedbackHtml: That is not an improvement.

answers.textHtml: It assigns blame without a process change
answers.feedbackHtml: That may not reduce recurrence.

answers.textHtml: It remains an undated suggestion
answers.feedbackHtml: Delivery cannot be assessed.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Lessons should become operating capability.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q06
questions.promptHtml: How should the Transnet public restoration statement be used?

answers.textHtml: As evidence of the reported restoration milestone
answers.feedbackHtml: Keep the example within its documented outcome.

answers.textHtml: As proof of every final forensic conclusion
answers.feedbackHtml: The statement's scope is narrower.

answers.textHtml: As a universal recovery-time requirement
answers.feedbackHtml: A case does not set that requirement.

answers.textHtml: As evidence that continuity planning is unnecessary
answers.feedbackHtml: The opposite lesson is to assess readiness.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Keep the example within its documented outcome.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which items need reconciliation after the scenario's restore? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: The possibly sent bank batch
answers.feedbackHtml: Its actual effect must be known.

answers.textHtml: The 120 paper applications
answers.feedbackHtml: They must join the restored service accurately.

answers.textHtml: Only the restored database's row total, without joining the pending work
answers.feedbackHtml: An aggregate does not resolve the actual outstanding applications and payment effects.

answers.textHtml: All transactions entered again as new requests without checking their prior state
answers.feedbackHtml: Blind re-entry can duplicate completed work.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Reconcile work across all continuity channels.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which questions belong in a response review? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Were decision owners and contacts reachable?
answers.feedbackHtml: Coordination affects response.

answers.textHtml: Did alternative service and evidence preservation work?
answers.feedbackHtml: Both influence harm and recovery.

answers.textHtml: How can all uncertainty be removed from the history?
answers.feedbackHtml: The history should remain accurate.

answers.textHtml: How can the report replace actual improvements?
answers.feedbackHtml: The report should support delivery.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Review decisions and operating capability.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q09
questions.promptHtml: A review should retain successful response practices as well as failures.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Preserving what worked supports future capability.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Preserving what worked supports future capability.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Preserving what worked supports future capability.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q10
questions.promptHtml: Declaring normal operations resumed is solely a matter of changing a dashboard status.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. It requires the authorised recovery and service decision.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: It requires the authorised recovery and service decision.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: It requires the authorised recovery and service decision.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match each recovery element to its purpose.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Recovery and learning cover both service and control outcomes.

questions.name: M09-U02-Q12
questions.promptHtml: A lesson becomes capability through an owned [[1]] and an observed [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: An unimplemented recommendation is not yet a changed capability.
